commits.message:
docs: Windows host-OS memory exclusion demonstrated box-local (E3) [skip ci]

E3 (2026-10-23, nucbox-k11) demonstrated that the host OS cannot read a
VBS type-1 guest's private memory: a privileged host live memory capture
that DOES read a non-isolated child partition's guest RAM (clean guest-only
marker) does NOT contain a VBS-isolated child partition's guest-only secret
(same GPA-backed partitions, differing only in the isolation bit).

Updates README (intro caveat + Shield claims), PRODUCT public-claims status,
and verifier V8 from 'Windows host exclusion unproven / E3 parked' to
'host-OS memory exclusion demonstrated box-local'. Kept honest, scoped:
the per-app signed report still records host_excluded:no (box-local
demonstration, not report-attestable), protection from the physical
operator is not established (residual: a raw-SPA kernel-debugger read,
blocked by Secure Boot), and there is still no external audit.
Evidence: windows/vbslike/evidence/e3-host-memory-20261023/.

docs(README): host-OS exclusion is by the isolation mechanism (demonstrated), not separation alone; keep operator unexcluded [skip ci]

The intro caveat no longer lists the host OS in 'separation does not by
itself exclude ...': E3 (2026-10-23) demonstrated VBS isolation excludes
the host OS box-local. The clause keeps the operator (not excluded) and
the point that host-OS exclusion comes from the isolation mechanism, not
from per-app placement. Report host_excluded:no, box-local scope, and
no-external-audit limits retained.
docs(README): simpler wording for the protections paragraph [skip ci]
